boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Cape Girardeau record (April 26, 1863) in Marmaduke's Second Expedition into Missouri [April-May 1863]. The Patterson and Fredericktown skirmishes (April 20-22), Vandever's night attack near Jackson (April 26) and the retreat are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Garrison plus some reinforcements [US] and cavalry division [CS], with no numerical bounds; the live field reads 2000 (US 2000; CS 0). McNeil telegraphed that he was attacked by 8,000 men. Marmaduke says his whole strength was about 5,000 men with ten guns, of whom about 1,200 were unarmed and 900 dismounted, that he estimated McNeil's force at Bloomfield at about 2,000, and that Cape Girardeau was held by about 3,000 infantry and cavalry with four large forts. NPS gives McNeil's combined force as about 2,000.
claims.rationale: An interested enemy estimate, an interested own-strength figure with its armed/mounted qualification and a garrison estimate after reinforcement by water. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live CS zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Marmaduke says the country for at least 100 miles was without forage or subsistence and his horses were worn by forced marches, and that McNeil was heavily reinforced by water. McNeil asked for two infantry regiments, a battery and ammunition, and reported that two steamers with reinforcements had arrived. Kirby Smith's indorsement says the expedition was made chiefly because of the scarcity of forage in Arkansas.
claims.rationale: Interested reports and an indorsement; no supply return inspected.

Marmaduke and John McNeil; the live page lists Marmaduke without a rank.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports and a summary; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. McNeil reported that he had repulsed the attack. Marmaduke calls the action a demonstration and says he withdrew his columns toward Jackson. NPS says Marmaduke was repulsed.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The sides characterize the action differently.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 337 total (US 12; CS 325), as does the live field. No inspected report gives a loss for April 26: McNeil's dispatches give none, and Marmaduke's figure of some 30 killed, 60 wounded and 120 missing (read 'GO') covers the whole expedition, with the compiled addenda return garbled in OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen CS 325 has no inspected basis; the expedition total is not assigned to this record.

open_questions: McNeil's own report of the action (promised in his May 10 letter), Curtis's dispatches and addenda return (No. 1, read and not selected), Meisner's, Baumer's and Benjamin's reports (Nos. 4, 9-10), and Shelby's-brigade (Thompson, No. 14) and Carter's (No. 18) reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. McNeil's April 26, 1863 dispatches from Cape Girardeau and Vandever's April 30-May 4 dispatches are separate author families of interested Union accounts; Marmaduke's May 20, 1863 report is one family of interested Confederate accounts, and Kirby Smith's printed indorsement and the compiled addenda return (garbled in OCR) are not counted as further families. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
